_note: Pure-Python wheels the chapter 15 page embeds (template 9.44.0 unpacks them in the page's Python worker) so that ezsheets and the real google-api-python-client can run in the browser; Pyodide 0.28.2's own distribution has neither, but it does have the packages named in pyodide_packages, which the page loads first. Downloaded from PyPI with pip on 2026-10-12; the page-data builder refuses a file whose SHA-256 differs from the one recorded here. The wheels build requests and read answers; no example reaches Google. ezsheets is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later; the page embeds it unmodified together with its source distribution committed in 03-materials/ch15/assets. boot_python skips the docstring text that google-api-python-client builds for each method of each resource (Schemas.prettyPrintSchema and Schemas.prettyPrintByName return an empty string) (no request, answer or argument depends on it; it makes each example several times faster in the browser). It also defines _before_run(), which the Python worker calls before every program (template 9.44.0) and which puts ezsheets, the clock functions and the working folder back as they were at start, because the browser keeps one Python for many programs where the study ran a fresh interpreter for each. VERSION 9.95.0 (new file over 1.0.0): boot_python also writes the stand-in module google_standin (03-materials/ch15/assets/google_standin_v1_0_0.py, sha256 de417119b7033dad57005a69186fb1bc73a2d3524443e3fe54d6bf89894e9db5, the file named in the manifest's library block) into the browser Python's site-packages under that name and imports it (its speed patch replaces the skip of the older boot), because the 25 examples of the chapter-code tab import it; _before_run also puts the stand-in module back as it was. The wheels and Pyodide packages are those of 1.0.0, unchanged.
